_README: Where Harry actually stands right now. Used by the follow-up nudges to add
ONE true sentence about his timeline - nothing else reads this file.
Why it exists: what a candidate says about his own position is the easiest
thing in the world to overstate, so it is written down as facts with an
expiry rather than left to a model to phrase, and every rule below is
- The employer is NEVER named - not the one making an offer, not the one
he works for. In a market the size of Aberdeen's it gets straight back.
- It says a fact exists. It never says what it is worth, never invents a
competing bid, and never implies somebody else has offered more.
- decide_by is a hard expiry. Past that date the sentence disappears on
its own, because 'I have an offer' stops being true the moment he
- It is only ever added to a FOLLOW-UP, never a first approach. Leading
with leverage to somebody who has not met you reads as arrogance.
The offer this file used to describe was Hydro Group's, and he took it -
which is exactly what decide_by is for. 'employed' replaces it: weaker
than an offer, true for as long as the job lasts, and it does the useful
half of the same work by saying he is not desperate.

employed.note: Technician, Aberdeen. Employer deliberately not recorded - it is never named in an email, and least of all to another employer in the same city.

_interview_note: Set interview_booked when a date is known, as {"on": "YYYY-MM-DD"}.
The Leonardo interview (Manufacturing Technician / Principal Test
Technician, Edinburgh, via an agency) has no date on the invitation Harry
forwarded, so nothing is claimed here. 'on' is a hard expiry like
decide_by: past it, the sentence stops being used.
